title: Modernize SKU bundles & threshold cutover playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Execute a coordinated cutover from legacy per-feature SKUs and ad-hoc thresholds to the new bundle-based SKU model with explicit soft/hard limits, improved entitlements mapping, and billing-friendly identifiers. This ticket owns the cross-team orchestration (billing, backend, console, docs, sales enablement, and comms) and the playbook for the cutover weekend and post-cutover verification.
acceptance_criteria: New bundle SKUs live in the billing system and matched to entitlements (account-level) with correct rate plan IDs
Console displays new SKU names, per-route limits and rollover behavior in UI and in API responses
Billing export (CSV+parquet) contains both legacy_sku and new_bundle_sku fields for 30 days after cutover
Migration script idempotently maps existing customer usages to new thresholds with no double-billing incidents in a canary cohort
Sales and support have updated playbooks and FAQ before public comms
Release notes and customer-facing docs published at cutover and pinned for 7 days
rollout_plan: Week -4: Finalize SKU catalog and rate plan IDs; freeze public-facing names
Week -3: Billing integration dry-run (staging) with sample accounts; verify exports
Week -2: Console and API beta (internal+select customers); collect feedback
Week -1: Lock cutover runbook; tabletop with SRE, Billing, Sales Ops, Support
- 02:00: Quiesce pricing config writes (API access control for SKU updates)
- 02:15: Run migration step 1: create new bundle entries in billing producer (idempotent)
- 03:00: Run migration step 2: entitlement mapping job (sample canary accounts first)
- 04:00: Switch console and API feature-flag to show new SKUs
- 05:00: Unfreeze config writes; monitor for anomalous billing spikes
Post-cutover (first 72h): rolling verification across customer cohorts and usage-based checks
communication_plan: Internal (T-7 days): Dry-run notes and Slack briefing in #pricing-prod and #sre on the schedule
Support & Sales (T-5 days): Runbook walkthrough, objection handling FAQ, and canned email templates
Early-access customers (T-3 days): Private notice with migration timeline and opt-out instructions for manual mapping
Public release (Cutover day +0): Release notes, blog post, and updated docs; targeted customer emails for accounts affected by thresholds
Follow-up (Cutover day +7): Summary of cutover metrics to execs and a support war-room retrospective invite

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use bundle-first model (bundle + add-ons) rather than per-feature SKU to reduce catalog explosion; trade-off: short term migration complexity for long-term simplicity
Decision: Maintain legacy_sku column in exports for 30 days to aid reconciliation; trade-off: additional storage and export complexity
Tradeoff: Soft limits (alerts) vs hard enforcement on day 1. We will start with soft limits and billing warnings for 30 days to avoid breaking customer workloads.
Decision: Canary cohort of 5% of active customers for initial cutover to surface high-impact regressions before full rollout

risks_mitigations: Risk: Migration script double-applies usage leading to billing spike. Mitigation: idempotent job + pre-cutover dry-run against snapshot and canary cohort
Risk: Customer confusion from SKU name changes. Mitigation: keep legacy_sku mapping visible in invoices for 30 days and publish a clear mapping table
Risk: Console UI bug hides limits causing overage. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout, test plan, and emergency rollback path
Risk: Tax/invoice format regressions. Mitigation: Finance sign-off and sample invoices generated pre-cutover
post_release_followups: Cutover retrospective (T+7): collect incidents, edge cases, and metric deltas
Cleanup task (T+30): remove legacy_sku from active UI where safe and deprecate legacy export fields (announce 30d prior)
Billing reconciliation (T+14): compare expected vs actual revenue and surface discrepancies to Finance
Metrics: evaluate latency, billing export sizes, and support volume changes to measure impact
